chunks: As for the right of charity (sadaqa),

is that you know it is a storing away with your Lord and a deposit for which you will have no need for witnesses. If you deposit it in secret, you will be more confident of it than if you deposit it in public. And you should know that it repels afflictions and illnesses from you in this world, and it will repel the Fire from you in the next world.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly benefits of giving charity (sadaqa) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin frames charity not merely as a social duty but as a spiritual 'deposit' (wadi'a) with God, leveraging the concept of divine trustworthiness over human testimony to encourage sincerity. This passage underscores the dual efficacy of sadaqa as both a temporal shield against calamities (balaya) and an eschatological protection from the Fire, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the tangible spiritual benefits of righteous acts. The description of secret charity as more secure than public almsgiving aligns with the principle of hiding good deeds to preserve purity of intention (ikhlas).

en.william-c-chittick: The right of charity (sadaqa) is that you know it is a storing away with your Lord and a deposit for which you will have no need for witnesses.

If you deposit it in secret, you will be more confident of it than if you deposit it in public. [1] You should know that it repels afflictions and illnesses from you in this world and it will repel the Fire from you in the next world.
